memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Now the Israelites settled in Egypt in the region of Goshen. They acquired property there and were fruitful and increased greatly in number." — Gen 47:27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
One quiet sentence, and it carries enormous weight.

While all Egypt is selling its land to survive, Israel is acquiring property. While the region is wasting away, this family is becoming fruitful and increasing greatly in number. Seventy people walked into Goshen. A nation will walk out.

The words "fruitful and increased" deliberately echo God's command at creation, to be fruitful and increase in number (Gen 1:28). The narrator is telling us that God's original purpose for humanity is being carried forward through this particular family, in a foreign land, during the worst famine anyone could remember.

God's promises do not require favourable conditions. He had told Jacob at Beersheba, "I will make you into a great nation there" — in Egypt, in exile, in the very place that seemed like the wrong direction. And He is doing exactly that.

Do not measure God's faithfulness by how promising your surroundings look. He grows things in famines. He builds nations in foreign countries. He raised His Son in a tomb.

Whatever season you are in, He is not limited by it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you assumed God needs favourable conditions to work in your life?
2. Where has God grown something in you during a difficult season?
3. What promise of God are you struggling to believe because of your circumstances?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are not limited by my circumstances. Grow what You want to grow in me, even in a lean season, and help me trust Your faithfulness over my surroundings. Amen.
